podcast.body: This song is mentioned as part of Jefferson Starship's 70s music, with Grace Slick contributing harmonies and "oh babies" on a "deceptively raunchy part." "I love Jefferson Starship's 70s music, miracles, count on me, I love that."

This song reached number three on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming a massive radio hit for the band and a key track on their only number one album, *Red Octopus*. Marty Balin wrote and sang this song, making its recording a condition for his permanent return to the band. Its pop-friendly sound was a stark contrast to the band's 1960s counterculture identity, leading Grace Slick to feel "odd doing it like I was wearing a costume a monkey suit or something." "That's miracles made at number three on the billboard hot 100 in the album red octopus was the only number one album Jefferson starship ever had."
